$comment: The reviewed bridge from the design to this app's Android resource names. Hand-maintained,
not generated: transcribing a design to Android is a series of judgements (fractional px to
whole dp, color-mix() to a baked alpha byte, which ramp steps the app actually needs), and
this file is where those judgements are written down.
A token can come from either of two upstream files, and several come from both:
'css' / 'cssValue'  the variable in nocturne/styles.css — the theme's own token
'dc'                a literal string in app/Figure Drawing App.dc.html — the design's
own value, which is where anything the theme has no opinion about
(the pose stage, the overlays, the rail) actually comes from
Nothing reads this file at build or run time and no test asserts it. It is a reviewed record,
checked by reading the diff when a pull lands. See README.md in this folder for that loop.

source.themePinNote: The design embeds its own snapshot of Nocturne at this path. Verified byte-identical to the live design-system project on 2026-09-06; it can drift if the theme is retuned and the design is not re-pinned.

colors.note: The unfilled arc of the countdown ring. Named separately from neutral_800 because it is a role, not a step: it tracks whatever the system's 800 is. The design hard-codes the hex rather than using the variable, which is why it is pinned on both edges.
The system's hairline. Android has no color-mix(), so the 16% is baked into the alpha byte.

Selected chip fill. The 16% is the design's, not the theme's — styles.css only offers .btn-primary's 12% hover / 22% active, and the design's own chip() helper picks 16% for the selected state. The app follows the design.
Full-screen break overlay, and the design's number: Nocturne has no full-bleed scrim, only .dialog-backdrop at 50%.
Pause sheet. A touch more transparent than the break overlay, which is a full stop.

The pose stage, a shade under the app ground so the reference image reads as a lightbox. The design's own colour, hard-coded there rather than tokenised — Nocturne has no full-bleed media surface to name it on.

Rule-of-thirds guide, XML-time default before GridContrast has sampled a pose. The design draws it at 0.18 over a mock image; on a real photograph that vanished, so the app raised it to 0.35 and added the casing below. Deliberate — do not sync this one back down.
Light guide core, picked by GridContrast over a dark region. Same 0.18 to 0.35 raise as grid_line; the design has no light/dark variant at all, because it never sampled the image.
Dark guide core. Pure black rather than a Nocturne neutral — the guide has to survive over an arbitrary photograph, not over the app's own grounds.
Casing down each side of a dark core.
Casing down each side of a light core.

dimens.note: Rounds to 11dp; nudged up to 12dp to sit on Android's 4dp grid, where it is the standard content inset.
Rounds to 17dp; nudged down to 16dp for the same 4dp grid, and because 16dp is the platform's screen margin.
The design's chip() helper. Matches .btn-icon's 36px and .input's min-height, and clears the touch minimum.
The design's tab() helper. Nocturne's .nav is a desktop bar with no height floor; 52dp clears the 48dp touch minimum with room for a label.
Countdown ring. The design's SVG viewport; Nocturne has no equivalent.

Player rail beside the pose on a wide screen (fold open). The design draws it at 288px, where its four tool chips wrap to two rows; the app widened it to 328dp so they keep full-size labels in one row (below ~300dp Chip.Tool starts autosizing down). A real divergence — the design should probably follow the app here, not the other way round.
Gap between pips. The design uses 4px; the app tightened it to 3dp because a 12-pose session's pips wrap on a 412dp phone at 4dp. Cosmetic, and the smaller of the two divergences to care about.
Reference-grid cell. Shorter with the fold open, where there are four columns.
Guide core. A 1dp hairline was too thin to read against a photograph.
Casing each side of the core.

unusedCss.--color-accent-2: Nocturne's secondary accent. The app is single-accent; a second one would need a role first.
unusedCss.--color-accent-100: Ramp step no screen uses yet.
unusedCss.--color-accent-500: Ramp step no screen uses yet.
unusedCss.--color-accent-600: Ramp step no screen uses yet.
unusedCss.--color-accent-700: Ramp step no screen uses yet.
unusedCss.--color-accent-800: Tag background in Nocturne; the app has no tags.
unusedCss.--color-accent-900: Ramp step no screen uses yet.
unusedCss.--color-neutral-100: Ramp step no screen uses yet.
unusedCss.--color-neutral-200: Ramp step no screen uses yet.
unusedCss.--color-neutral-700: Ramp step no screen uses yet.
unusedCss.--color-section: Deck-scale fill for slide dividers. Nocturne marks these as not interface colors.
unusedCss.--font-heading: Reaches the app as the bundled Inter at Resources/font/, wired through the theme's textAppearance rather than as a token. TypefaceContractTests guards it.
unusedCss.--font-body: Same as --font-heading: one family, both roles.
unusedCss.--font-heading-weight: Inter 500, bundled at Resources/font/ and selected by the textAppearance styles.
unusedCss.--space-1: 2.8px. Below the point where a dp value stays meaningful; the app's tightest gap is pip_gap at 3dp.
unusedCss.--radius-sm: 4px. No control in the app is smaller than radius_md.
unusedCss.--shadow-sm: Nocturne's elevation is a hairline outline plus an ambient shadow, which Android expresses as a stroked drawable plus elevation rather than a colour token.

$pendingComment: Decisions the design has made that the Android app has not built yet. The design runs ahead of
the app — that is what a design is for — but an unbuilt decision is easy to lose, so each one
is pinned to the literal that carries it in the design file, so a pull's diff shows when the
designer drops the idea and the entry can be revisited rather than quietly outliving it.

pendingFromDesign.what: Countdown ring turns pale violet in the last 10 seconds
pendingFromDesign.detail: The design swaps the ring stroke to #c7bff0 and the clock text to --color-accent-300 while warn10 is on, the phase is 'pose' and remaining <= 10. The app has neither colour: colors.xml has no #c7bff0, and nothing reads a warning state.

pendingFromDesign.what: Break overlay carries a skip button
pendingFromDesign.detail: The design's break overlay has a 'Next image' button that ends the break early.

pendingFromDesign.what: Blur tool on the pose viewer
pendingFromDesign.detail: The design's rail has a fourth tool chip, Blur, at 6px. The app's rail has Grayscale, Flip and Grid. No ticket yet — this is the clearest unticketed gap between design and app.

pendingFromDesign.what: Zoom controls on the pose viewer
pendingFromDesign.detail: The design has − / + chips stepping scale by 0.2 between 1 and 2.5. No ticket yet.
